questions.q: What must a server do before trusting claims inside a JWT?
o: Decode the payload from Base64URL back into JSON
Confirm the raw token is longer than 100 characters
Verify the signature with the expected secret or key
Check the request Content-Type before reading cookies
questions.x: Decoding only reveals the claims. Verification checks that the signature was produced with the expected secret or private key. If the server skips that check, a modified payload is treated as authentic.
questions.h: Reading the payload needs no key. Which step actually proves the token was issued legitimately?

questions.q: If a server never checks signatures, what is enough to forge a JWT?
o: Crack the HMAC secret with an offline wordlist attack
Edit the payload claims, then Base64URL-encode them again
Generate a new RSA key pair and publish it to JWKS
Break TLS so the signing key can be read from the wire
questions.x: No key is needed. Decode the payload, change a claim such as sub, re-encode it, and send the token. The header and original signature can stay untouched because the server never checks them.
questions.h: The server never looks at the signature. Do you still need the signing key, or only a readable payload?

questions.q: After the payload is changed, what is true of the original signature?
o: It no longer matches, but a skip-verify server still accepts it
The browser recalculates it before the request is sent
The server always rejects it because the HMAC no longer matches
HTTP middleware strips it automatically from the cookie
questions.x: The signature was computed over the original header and payload, so it is invalid for the new payload. A server that verifies would reject it. A server that only decodes accepts it anyway.
questions.h: The signature is now wrong for the new content. Does the vulnerable server ever look at that mismatch?

questions.q: What is the none algorithm attack against JWT verification?
o: Leaving the payload unencrypted so anyone can read the claims
Removing the header so the verifier has no algorithm to check
Putting a null byte in kid so path checks stop at the first key
Setting alg to none so the server skips signature checking
questions.x: Some libraries accept alg none, which disables signature checking. An attacker sets alg to none and sends header.payload. with an empty signature, or header.payload. plus any garbage signature.
questions.h: Some JWT libraries treat one alg value as meaning unsigned. What is that value?

questions.q: Why is calling decode() instead of verify() dangerous for authentication?
o: decode() is slower because it always fetches keys over the network
decode() parses the token but does not check the signature at all
verify() supports only RS256, so decode() is required for HS256
decode() is deprecated and always throws in production builds
questions.x: Libraries often split decoding from verifying. decode() only parses the structure. Using it for authentication skips signature validation, so forged payloads are trusted as long as they parse as JSON.
questions.h: One method is for reading the token. The other is for trusting it. Which one skips the signature?
